newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit eases sharply on fresh selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit eases sharply on fresh selling pressure.

text.p: The ringgit logged fresh losses on Monday afternoon as selling pressure increased on dollar demand from the corporate sector, dealers said.
They said the ringgit lost nearly 200 points to 2.7900 to a dollar by the time London opened for trading.
However, volumes were extremely thin, which were exaggerating the movement, the dealers said.
"Even one or two (million) dollars transaction is causing a 30-point movement," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said the pressure was expected to continue in the near-term though topside for dollar was limited at 2.7950.
Dealers said the central Bank Negara continued to monitor movements in dollar/ringgit, but was staying out of the market.

"Everyone is just executing orders. No interbank player is holding big positions," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore. "We are seeing some genuine customer flows both ways but market is choppy because of thin volumes."
"While general view is still bullish (dollar), there could be some correction in the near-term," he said.
He said if 2.75 to a dollar broke, the ringgit could gain to 2.65. On the upside, 2.8250, its new low since flotation in 1973, was expected to hold.
